expectations.text: Output contains a mechanical identity / decomposition section
expectations.evidence: Has '## Mechanical Identity' with core loops, resource dynamics, tension structure, progression arc, interaction model, perspective/pacing, and a mechanical identity statement.

expectations.text: At least 5 distinct setting concepts are presented
expectations.evidence: 7 settings: The Oral Examination (★★★★★), The Negotiations Table (★★★★★), Succession (★★★★★), The Pitch Circuit (★★★★), The Immigration Case (★★★★★), The Campaign Trail (★★★★), The Residency (★★★★).

expectations.text: At least one setting moves completely away from the corporate/career metaphor
expectations.evidence: Multiple non-corporate settings: The Oral Examination (academia/dissertation defense), The Immigration Case (legal/immigration attorney), The Residency (medical residency), The Negotiations Table (labor organizing). All have completely different social contexts despite using the same mechanics.

expectations.text: The recommendations section explicitly discusses whether to lean satirical or sincere, with reasoning
expectations.evidence: The Campaign Trail is explicitly 'Not recommended for this brief' because 'Political games trend satirical so easily that executing a sincere, non-satirical political deckbuilder would require extraordinary discipline. This is exactly the opposite of what you asked for.' The Pitch Circuit is also flagged: 'Startup culture has been satirized so thoroughly... that a sincere take would read as naive rather than earnest.'

expectations.text: Each setting's Mechanical Mapping explains what 'drawing cards' and 'building a deck' means in that world
expectations.evidence: All 7 settings ground the deck in the fiction: 'Deck = your dissertation's argumentative structure', 'Deck = your organizing toolkit' (direct conversations, public actions, grievance filings), 'Deck = your relationship and reputation toolkit' (family politics), 'Deck = your legal and procedural toolkit', etc.

expectations.text: At least 2 settings explicitly address what the two run-end states (failure vs. success) mean thematically
expectations.evidence: All 7 settings address both end states. Examples: Oral Examination: 'Fired = dissertation rejected. Promoted out = you pass and must leave academia for the world beyond — bittersweet.' Immigration Case: 'Fired (lose condition) = client deported. Promoted out (win condition) = case granted; they leave your caseload into a better life.'

notes: Perfect score. The skill pushed well beyond corporate metaphor into genuinely unexpected territory (immigration law, academia, labor organizing). The sincerity/satire tension from the user's prompt was directly addressed in the recommendations.
